title: Material alteration: surprise and hardship
summary: The commentary’s surprise-or-hardship language produces both factual inquiries and disagreement about the legal test.
notes: Bayway requires attention to subjective and objective surprise and holds that industry practice defeated the claimed objective surprise. It expressly declines to decide whether hardship is an independent ground because the evidence was insufficient either way. Union Carbide’s quoted view treats hardship as a consequence rather than a separate criterion. Some cases deem particular terms material categorically; Dorton treats its arbitration question as fact dependent. Preserve those differences.

sources.label: Farnsworth et al., Contracts: Cases and Materials, 10th ed. (2023), pp. 284–290. Open assigned page 284.
